title: Localization of cohomology of a derived tensor
statement: Let R\to A and R\to R' be maps of commutative rings, put A'=A\otimes_R R', and let M be a complex of A-modules [def-pc-ring-tensor-cohomology]. For a prime q' of A' with images q in A, p' in R' and p in R, there is a natural isomorphism H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L} R')\otimes_{A'}A'_{q'} \cong H^i(M_q\otimes_{R_p}^{\mathbf L} R'_{p'})\otimes_{A_q\otimes_{R_p}R'_{p'}}A'_{q'} for every i, where the A-action on the left is induced by endomorphisms of M in D(A) and the right side uses the localized complex. Derived cohomology, its coefficient actions, and the comparison map are interpreted using [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model], applied to a functorial K-flat A-resolution of M and its localization. The isomorphism is compatible with morphisms of M and with the canonical comparison map to M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L} A'.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat $A$-complex $P^\bullet\to M$ and a K-flat $R$-complex $F^\bullet\to R'$. By [lem-pc-balanced-derived-tensor-model], $C=\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_R F^\bullet)$ represents $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ in $D(A)$, with an $A'$-action on its cohomology, not a strict $A'$-complex structure. Regard a ring $\Lambda$ as a ringed one-point space; for the morphisms of ringed one-point spaces given by $A\to A_q$ and $R\to R_p$ the pullback is termwise $-\otimes_A A_q$, resp. $-\otimes_R R_p$, so [lem-pc-kflat-pullback-preservation] makes $P_q$ and $F_p$ K-flat over $A_q$ and $R_p$, and exact localization preserves the quasi-isomorphisms $P_q\to M_q$, $F_p\to R'_p$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Termwise, $(P\otimes_R F)_q=P_q\otimes_R F$ (associativity of $A_q\otimes_A-$), and since $R\setminus p$ acts bijectively on the $R_p$-module $P_q$, the tensor-localization formula [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] (with $S=R\setminus p$, $\ell_{P_q}=\mathrm{id}$, $\ell_F:F\to F_p$) identifies $P_q\otimes_R F$ with $P_q\otimes_{R_p}F_p$ by pure tensors; so $C_q\cong\operatorname{Tot}(P_q\otimes_{R_p}F_p)$, which represents $M_q\otimes_{R_p}^{\mathbf L}R'_p$ by the same balanced-model lemma (over $R_p$, with $A_q$ and $R'_p$).

source.place: Tag 0DJ8, affine proof, choice of K-flat model and localization of the derived tensor complex

proof.text: The pure-tensor identification of Step 1 commutes with differentials and is natural in the second factor (a chain map $F\to F'$ of $R$-complexes and its localization). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], $H^i(C)\otimes_A A_q=H^i(C_q)$. This is an identity of $A_q\otimes_{R_p}R'_p$-modules: the $A$-action is multiplication on $P$, and the action of $b\in R'$ is the endomorphism of $R'$ in $D(R)$ given by multiplication by $b$, as specified by [lem-pc-derived-tensor-action-naturality]; a roof $F\leftarrow\tilde F\to F$ of K-flat $R$-complexes representing it localizes (exactly, by the same two cited lemmas) to a roof representing multiplication by $b/1$ on $R'_p$ in $D(R_p)$, so the actions correspond. Applying the same identification to $F\to R'$ shows that the comparison map of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-action-naturality], $P\otimes_R F\to P\otimes_R R'$, localizes at $q$ to the comparison map $P_q\otimes_{R_p}F_p\to P_q\otimes_{R_p}R'_p$ for $R_p\to A_q$, $R_p\to R'_p$; naturality in $M$ holds because every map is induced by a chain map $P\to P'$ of K-flat models.

source.place: Tag 0DJ8, affine proof, displayed localization identity and compatibility with the comparison map

proof.text: The map $R'_p\to R'_{p'}$ is a flat localization. Apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-flat-second-localization] with base ring $R_p$, first algebra $A_q$, second algebra $R'_p$, and its localization $R'_{p'}$: it identifies $H^i(M_q\otimes_{R_p}^{\mathbf L}R'_p)\otimes_{R'_p}R'_{p'}$ with $H^i(M_q\otimes_{R_p}^{\mathbf L}R'_{p'})$ as $A_q\otimes_{R_p}R'_{p'}$-modules, naturally in $M$ and compatibly with the comparison maps. Since $A'_{q'}$ is a localization of $A_q\otimes_{R_p}R'_{p'}$, which is a localization of $A'$ (the elements of $A\setminus q$ and $R'\setminus p'$ map outside $q'$), transitivity of module localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] gives $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R')\otimes_{A'}A'_{q'}=(H^i(C)\otimes_A A_q\otimes_{R'}R'_{p'})\otimes_{A_q\otimes_{R_p}R'_{p'}}A'_{q'}$, and Step 2 with the isomorphism above turns this into the displayed isomorphism. Compatibility with morphisms of $M$ and with the comparison map to $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ follows from the naturality and comparison-map clauses of Step 2 and of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-flat-second-localization], localized at $q'$.
